spring_2027_deadline: 2026-10-01 (October 1 spring deadline per NUSC Graduate Admissions page and NUSC MS/PhD FAQ dated 2022-12-07; no separate international date seen) - PASSED as of 2026-10-11
fall_2027_deadline: February 15 (standing fall deadline per NUSC FAQ and NUSC Graduate Admissions page; for Fall 2027 this would be 2027-02-15 - sources are 2021-2022 era, confirm with department)
funding_deadline_note: No separate funding deadline seen. Assistantships are awarded by individual faculty advisors; FAQ advises contacting faculty about funding before applying. Graduate School fellowships are selected through the Slate application.
ielts_subscore_note: No subscore minimum seen on Graduate School page. Online IELTS accepted; IELTS One Skill Retake, General Training and Indicator not accepted. Official scores must come directly from the testing agency.
toefl_min: iBT 79 (old scale) or 4.5 (new scale); also PTE 60, Duolingo 110
funding_summary: NUSC FAQ: 'There are graduate assistantships available for students accepted into MS or PhD in Nutritional Sciences program. We offer research assistantships (RA) and teaching assistantships (TA).' Competitive and distributed at the faculty advisor's discretion; RA/TA at 50%-100% provides a stipend and waives tuition (student fees not waived). Applicants must ask individual faculty whether they have funding for a new student.
notes: NUSC graduate handbook: a major advisor must be determined before a student is accepted; applicants name a preferred faculty advisor in the application. Department does not waive the application fee, but an accepting faculty member may cover it (FAQ). GRE not required since the Fall 2022 cycle (NUSC admissions page). International students needing a visa must submit materials to ISSS at least one month before classes start. Spring 2027 is closed; target Fall 2027 and contact faculty about funding first. Program sources are 2021-2022 era; confirm dates.

program_name: PhD in Public Health (Social and Behavioral Sciences track verified)
department_or_school: Yale School of Public Health; degree through Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GSAS)
spring_2027_deadline: Not verified (no spring entry found; GSAS application is described as for Fall 2027 entry)
fall_2027_deadline: December 1 (YSPH PhD page: 'The application deadline, beginning with applicants applying for Fall 2026 admissions is December 1st'; for Fall 2027 this implies 2026-12-01 - confirm on GSAS)
funding_deadline_note: All admitted PhD students are funded; no separate funding deadline seen.
ielts_subscore_note: Conflicting sources: YSPH 'How to Apply & FAQ's' page lists IELTS 7.0 as the minimum; GSAS 'Guidance for International Students' lists 'IELTS: 8.0 or higher' and says GSAS itself has no test minimums (departments may set them). Either way above the applicant's 6.5.
funding_summary: GSAS: 'All PhD students at Yale receive a fellowship that covers the full cost of tuition ($52,400 for 2026-2027), a 12-month stipend (minimum of $52,046 for 2026-2027), and comprehensive health insurance, typically for at least five years.' YSPH: all PhD students are guaranteed five years of 12-month stipend and tuition support (fellowships, teaching fellowships, traineeships, research assistantships).
notes: GRE: GSAS Public Health page says 'GRE is not accepted for: Social and Behavioral Sciences (PhD)'; GRE policy for other PhD tracks not verified. Writing sample not required; GSAS GRE/TOEFL code 3987; application portal opens August 15. Fully funded but very competitive, and the IELTS bar (7.0+) is above her 6.5. Nutrition faculty member Rafael Pérez-Escamilla is in Social and Behavioral Sciences.
